title: EXP-057 — Hello World Part 3 Section 8: FX_Items Saved Definition Recovery and Runtime Set Values Verification
objective: Recover the existing User-scoped FX_Items Form in Web Designer through a bounded native navigation sequence, verify that the saved Prompt and Set Values actions, variable-bound Edit, original components, and Initial Command remain present, and independently record whether FX_VarTest exists as a Form-variable definition. Then reopen the existing FX_Items Web Client runtime Form once, capture its automatic Hello World prompt, and observe the displayed FX_VarTestEdit value against the currently selected item's FX_Description. Perform exactly one native FX_Refresh activation, capture the second Hello World prompt and resulting value, and optionally observe what happens when selecting the eggs row without another refresh. Do not recreate, edit, or save any Form metadata or business records. Classify conclusions as observed recovery and runtime behavior only, not replay verification or independently proven database durability.

in_scope: T1 read-only preflight: enumerate browser tabs before selecting either browser page; establish the inherited Designer empty-canvas state and User editing scope, and inspect the inherited Web Client FX_Items runtime tab without altering it.
Inspect EXP-056 T8 through T10 evidence to establish the previously saved handler, Edit binding, exact scoped identity, native Save result, and failed reopening boundary.

T2 Designer recovery: use the native Form menu recent-forms FX_Items entry. Open the menu, obtain a fresh snapshot, then attempt the visible entry once. If it times out, permit exactly one retry after reopening the menu and capturing fresh visibility evidence.

If both recent-forms attempts fail, permit exactly one alternative through the documented native Designer Open toolbar and Select Form dialog, filtering for FX_Items and selecting only the exact intended Form.
Verify recovered Form Name FX_Items, ScopeType User, and ScopeName matching the EXP-056 saved baseline before accepting any recovered-definition evidence.

Inspect Initial Command Refresh, exactly one StdFormRefreshCompleted handler group, sequence 0 Prompt with Hello World and OK response, and sequence 1 Set Values with SETVARVALUES(FX_VarTest=P(FX_Description)).

Inspect the saved component inventory, including the original 16 components, FX_RefreshButton, FX_DescriptionEdit, and exactly one FX_VarTestEdit with Binding Type Variable and Binding variables.FX_VarTest.
Independently inspect the Designer Variables tab for FX_VarTest. Record its presence and exposed definition attributes, or its absence, without creating or repairing a definition.

T3 runtime: close the inherited clean FX_Items runtime Form tab once, open FX_Items once through native Web Client Open > Select Form, and capture the automatic Hello World Prompt before dismissing it through one authorized OK response.
Observe FX_VarTestEdit's displayed value, currently selected item identity, and the corresponding FX_Description value using native rendered UI and accessibility evidence.
T4 runtime: click FX_Refresh exactly once, capture the resulting Hello World Prompt, dismiss with one authorized OK, and observe FX_VarTestEdit and the corresponding Description again.
Optionally select the existing eggs row without modifying it or activating refresh again, and record whether FX_VarTestEdit changes, remains unchanged, clears, or displays an error.
Capture screenshots, accessibility snapshots, controlled-action counts, acceptance evidence, and limitations under evidence/EXP-057/.
Write or update only the EXP-057 experiment record and its evidence directory. Leave existing Mongoose artifacts unchanged.
out_of_scope: Replaying EXP-056 or recreating its Set Values handler, variable target, Edit component, or existing FX_Items Form.
Testing a second Designer Save or changing saved Form metadata.
Creating a distinct FX_VarTest Form-variable definition to compensate for its previously observed absence.
Repairing missing, invalid, or unresolved variable bindings.
Testing other Forms, IDOs, databases, event handlers, or component types.
Changing the FX_Items SQL table, IDO, property classes, or any business records.
General-purpose Designer navigation troubleshooting beyond the specifically authorized reopening sequence.
Independent database durability, cache-eviction, cross-session authentication persistence, or FormSync serialization claims.
Additional runtime refresh activations, repeated runtime openings, or manual triggering of other Form events.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Do not create, delete, rename, move, resize, or edit any Mongoose Form, component, variable definition, event, handler action, IDO, property class, SQL table, or business record.
Do not invoke Designer Save, Regenerate Form, Undo, Redo, or any other metadata-committing operation.
Do not create FX_VarTest through Details > Variables > New or alter its Persistent, Global, or Value properties.
Do not change either StdFormRefreshCompleted action, its Parameters, sequence, event name, or enabled state.
Do not type into FX_VarTestEdit or any other runtime data-entry component.
Do not invoke runtime Save, Delete, New Record, or any operation that changes business data.
Do not click FX_Refresh more than once in EXP-057.
Do not open the runtime FX_Items Form more than once after the inherited tab is closed.
Do not dismiss more than one Hello World Prompt for each authorized activation. If additional prompts or unexpected dialogs appear, record the state and stop.
Do not exceed two recent-forms reopening attempts or one alternative Designer Open toolbar attempt.
Do not use direct MGForm URLs, browser navigation, browser refresh, client restart, session replacement, or deliberate login or reauthentication.
Do not invoke diagnostic controls, User Preferences, cache unload, FormSync, check-in, check-out, SQL, hidden APIs, internal stores, JavaScript injection, or scripts.

Do not perform speculative recovery or expand the experiment scope following an error. Allow at most one fresh recovery snapshot and one corrected inspection for a browser-reference failure, separate from the explicitly approved native reopening attempts.
Do not modify AGENTS.md, environment records, recipes, previous experiment records, or evidence from EXP-056.

acceptance_checks.description: Read-only preflight establishes the inherited browser tabs before first selection, the empty Designer Form-tab list, clean Designer controls, exact User editing scope, and the existing Web Client FX_Items runtime state. Capture separate Designer and runtime screenshots and accessibility snapshots, and reconcile them with EXP-056's final state.

Exactly one FX_Items Designer Form is successfully opened through the authorized native recovery sequence. Evidence records each attempted route, result, and retry count. The loaded Form is independently identified by Name FX_Items, ScopeType User, and the exact EXP-056 ScopeName, with Save disabled and no error dialog. Failure to recover the intended scoped Form blocks all subsequent definition and runtime work.

The recovered FX_Items Designer definition visibly retains Initial Command Refresh and exactly one StdFormRefreshCompleted handler group containing sequence 0 Prompt with its original Hello World and OK configuration and sequence 1 Set Values with the exact summary SETVARVALUES(FX_VarTest=P(FX_Description)). Capture the handler grid and native parameter readback without editing.

The recovered component inventory contains exactly the original 16 components plus one FX_VarTestEdit. The recovered Edit's properties establish Name FX_VarTestEdit, Type Edit, Binding Type Variable, Binding variables.FX_VarTest, Location 12.7222222222222; 30.25, Size 37.05; 2, and unchanged Events. FX_RefreshButton and the original FX_DescriptionEdit remain present with their expected properties. Compare the original inventory against EXP-056 evidence and explicitly record unavailable fields.

After the Designer recovery, the Variables tab is independently inspected for a distinct FX_VarTest Form-variable definition. Capture either its presence and all exposed fields or its absence with Form-category and filtered evidence. Both results satisfy this observation-only check; the outcome must not be inferred from the Set Values assignment or Edit binding. The Designer remains clean with Save disabled.

The clean inherited FX_Items Web Client runtime tab is closed exactly once, and FX_Items is opened exactly once using native Open > Select Form. The opening automatically produces the Hello World Prompt, which is captured before a single authorized OK dismissal. Evidence identifies the actual runtime Form and records closure, opening, and prompt-response counts.

After the initial runtime prompt is dismissed, capture the displayed FX_VarTestEdit value and the currently selected item's actual FX_Description in the same evidence sequence. For dumbbell, the expected Description is '45 pound iron'; for eggs, 'cage free'; for guitar, 'natural acoustic'. Exact equality between the displayed Edit value and the selected row's Description is required for this check. A blank value, mismatch, missing component, or visible error is recorded as a failed functional observation, not repaired.

Exactly one native FX_Refresh activation is performed. Its Hello World Prompt is captured before one authorized OK dismissal. After dismissal, FX_VarTestEdit and the selected row's Description are read again, with exact comparison and before/after evidence. The check passes only if the second activation and prompt are observed and the displayed Edit value equals the selected Description.

Record the unchanged original three item records and the runtime Save-disabled state. If the optional eggs-row selection is performed, capture the selected eggs Description and FX_VarTestEdit value before and after selection without another refresh. Treat any value change, non-change, or error as an observation; optional row selection is not itself a required success condition. No data mutations or extra refresh operations may occur.

Final evidence reconciles the exact Designer recovery attempts, one inherited runtime tab closure, one runtime opening, two expected Hello World Prompt observations, at most one OK dismissal per prompt, one FX_Refresh click, zero Designer Saves, zero metadata mutations, and zero business-data modifications. Any deviations are explicitly documented.

The final report provides a complete acceptance matrix with evidence references, observed versus unresolved findings, and a repository confinement audit showing only the EXP-057 experiment record and evidence/EXP-057/ changed. The outcome is classified as observed or blocked as supported; no replay_verified, independent database durability, or cache-eviction claim is made.

initial_instruction: EXP-057 T1 — READ-ONLY PREFLIGHT ONLY. Review AGENTS.md and the EXP-056 T8, T9, and T10 reports, including the documented last browser state and saved Form identity. List the controlled browser tabs BEFORE the first tab selection; capture the tab enumeration and identify the existing Web Client and Designer pages without assuming their order. Inspect the Designer through the supported browser UI and record its current Form-tab list, empty or nonempty canvas, User editing scope, Save state, dialogs, and session challenges. Separately inspect the inherited Web Client FX_Items runtime tab read-only: Form identity, current selected item, Description, FX_Refresh control, existing Edit visibility if any, original records, and Save state. Capture decisive screenshots and accessibility snapshots in evidence/EXP-057/ and write a concise T1 report with exact browser actions, observed versus inferred state, and blockers. Do not close or open a Form, interact with a Prompt, invoke a Designer menu reopening route, activate FX_Refresh, make any edit, or alter browser/session state during T1. Stop after documenting preflight. If the inherited pages or scopes conflict with the expected EXP-056 final state, record the discrepancy and stop without attempting recovery.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261011-163026-Hdng. Rationale: EXP-056 successfully saved a second StdFormRefreshCompleted action, SETVARVALUES(FX_VarTest=P(FX_Description)), and an Edit component FX_VarTestEdit bound to variables.FX_VarTest. Its immediate post-Save inspection confirmed both definitions, but the experiment was blocked when its single recent-forms reopen attempt timed out before the Form opened. EXP-057 is a separately authorized continuation, not a replay or recreation. It uses a newly specified, bounded native Designer reopening procedure and then observes whether the previously saved definitions survive reopening and function at runtime. This addresses the outstanding learning questions without another Designer Save, metadata mutation, or business-data modification. The ordinary Save and clean Form closure were performed in EXP-056; this experiment measures recovery of those existing artifacts rather than repeating their creation lifecycle. | Operator review 2026-10-11: narrowed the broad create/edit pattern (the verb "edit" matched the component type "Edit") and removed MGForm= from the navigation pattern (ordinary URL text); added the browser-JavaScript pattern, exact_values FX_Items, deny_browser_javascript, User editing scope. Approved by the operator 2026-10-11 with precondition attestation: logged in, configuration OK, Web Client loaded, no unsaved changes.
